coordinate_system: Planetocentric. Latitude N+, longitude E+ (-180..180; NASA's 0..360 values converted).

items.name: Viking 1
items.data_provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Mars Orbital Data Explorer)
items.description: First successful US Mars landing. Photographed the surface, analyzed the air and ran biology experiments.
items.fate: A bad software command ended contact in 1982, and nobody could repair it.
items.short_description: NASA's first successful Mars lander, searching for life in 1976.

quiz.question: In what year did Viking 1 land on Mars?
What ended contact with Viking 1 in 1982?
quiz.answer: A bad software command that could not be repaired

items.name: Viking 2
items.data_provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Mars Orbital Data Explorer)
items.description: Tracked Martian weather, studied soil chemistry and tested for life in Utopia Planitia.
items.short_description: Twin of Viking 1, studying weather and soil in Utopia Planitia.
items.key_fact: Studied Mars weather and tested the soil for life

quiz.question: Which Martian plain did Viking 2 explore?
What ended the Viking 2 mission in 1980?
wrong_answers: It got stuck in soft sand

items.name: Pathfinder + Sojourner
items.data_provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Mars Orbital Data Explorer)
items.description: Sojourner was the first wheeled rover on Mars; the airbag landing proved low-cost planetary entry.
items.fate: The lander’s battery ran down and contact faded in 1997.
items.short_description: Airbag-landed lander that deployed Sojourner, the first Mars rover.

quiz.question: What did Sojourner achieve on Mars?
quiz.answer: It was the first wheeled rover on the planet
wrong_answers: It was the first helicopter to fly there
It found water ice under the soil

quiz.question: Which low-cost landing method did Pathfinder prove?

items.name: Spirit
items.data_provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Mars Orbital Data Explorer)
items.note: Cartographic triangulation value. Doppler radio-tracking value: 14.571892 S, 175.47848 E.
items.description: Explored Gusev Crater and found evidence of past liquid water.
items.fate: Stuck in soft sand, it ran out of power in the 2010 Martian winter.
items.short_description: Rover that found signs of past water in Gusev Crater.
items.key_fact: Found evidence of past liquid water

quiz.question: What trapped Spirit before it lost power in the 2010 winter?
wrong_answers: A broken wheel on a boulder

items.name: Opportunity
items.data_provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Mars Orbital Data Explorer)
items.note: Cartographic triangulation value. Doppler radio-tracking value: 1.9483 S, 354.47417 E.
items.description: Worked nearly 15 years in Meridiani Planum and discovered clay minerals.
items.fate: A 2018 global dust storm blocked its sunlight; the mission ended in 2019.
items.short_description: Long-lived rover that worked in Meridiani Planum for nearly 15 years.
items.key_fact: Found clay minerals and worked nearly 15 years

quiz.question: About how long did Opportunity work on Mars?

items.name: Phoenix
items.data_provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Mars Orbital Data Explorer)
items.description: Dug into Martian arctic soil and confirmed water ice below the surface.
items.fate: Built for one summer, it could not survive the dark polar winter.
items.short_description: Arctic lander that dug up and confirmed Martian water ice.
items.key_fact: Confirmed water ice below the surface

quiz.question: What did Phoenix confirm beneath the Martian arctic soil?
Why could Phoenix not survive past its summer mission?

items.name: InSight
items.data_provider: NASA/JPL InSight team (Golombek et al. 2020, HiRISE-georeferenced)
items.description: Recorded marsquakes and measured the interior and heat of Mars.
items.fate: Dust covered its solar panels and it powered down in 2022.
items.short_description: Stationary lander that listened for marsquakes.

quiz.question: What did InSight record on Mars?
What covered InSight's solar panels and ended its mission in 2022?

items.name: Ingenuity
items.data_provider: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (Mars24 Sunclock, Mars Lander Missions list)
items.note: NASA lists Mars 2020 (Perseverance and the Ingenuity helicopter) at Octavia E. Butler Landing, Jezero Crater, to 0.01 degrees (about 600 m). Ingenuity's first airfield, Wright Brothers Field, is next to that landing site.
items.description: First powered, controlled aircraft to fly on another planet. It was planned for 5 test flights and flew 72 times, scouting terrain for Perseverance.
items.fate: A rotor blade was damaged on its 72nd landing in January 2024, so it could never fly again.
items.short_description: Small helicopter that proved powered flight on Mars.
items.key_fact: First helicopter to fly on another planet

quiz.question: Ingenuity was planned for 5 test flights. How many did it actually fly?
What ended Ingenuity's flying career in January 2024?
quiz.answer: A rotor blade damaged on its 72nd landing
